notes.b: Hormonal manipulation is the deliberate use of natural or synthetic hormones, or of drugs that block hormones, to change how an organism grows or functions.

points: Anabolic steroids are synthetic derivatives of testosterone. They increase muscle mass and strength and speed up recovery from training.

Anabolic steroids cause liver damage, increase the risk of heart disease, reduce sperm production, cause infertility and shrinking of the testes in males, cause male characteristics to develop in females, cause acne and cause mood changes including aggression.
EPO (erythropoietin) is a hormone made by the kidneys that stimulates red blood cell production.
Athletes misuse EPO to increase the oxygen-carrying capacity of the blood and so their endurance. The thickened blood increases the risk of clots, heart attack and stroke.
The World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) bans these substances in competitive sport and tests athletes through urine and blood samples. Their use is unfair to other competitors.
Insulin injections treat type 1 diabetes, in which the pancreas makes little or no insulin, so blood glucose would otherwise rise too high.
Most insulin used today is human insulin made by genetically modified bacteria (detail in Genetic Engineering).
The contraceptive pill contains synthetic oestrogen and progesterone, or progesterone alone.
The pill inhibits the release of FSH and LH, so no egg matures and ovulation is prevented.
Fertility treatment uses hormones to stimulate the ovaries to release eggs (detail in Human Reproduction).
Hormone replacement therapy (HRT) supplies oestrogen, often with progesterone, after the menopause to relieve symptoms such as hot flushes and to reduce bone loss.
For some women, HRT slightly increases the risk of some cancers and of blood clots.
Thyroxine tablets are given to people whose thyroid produces too little thyroxine.
Progesterone, given as a vaginal sponge or implant, synchronises the breeding cycles of cattle and sheep, so a herd can be bred and give birth at the same time.
Growth-promoting hormones increase meat production in cattle.
Bovine somatotropin (BST) increases milk yield in cattle.
Growth-promoting hormones and BST are banned in the EU, including Ireland, because of concerns about animal welfare and hormone residues in food. BST is permitted in the USA.
Synthetic auxins such as 2,4-D are selective weedkillers that kill broad-leaved weeds in cereal crops by making them grow uncontrollably.
Auxin rooting powder makes cuttings form roots.
Ethene gas is used to ripen fruit such as bananas in storage after transport.
Benefits: better health, treatment of disease, food production and convenience.
Costs: side effects, an unfair advantage in sport, animal welfare concerns, hormone residues in food and environmental effects of weedkillers.

keyTerms.definition: The deliberate use of natural or synthetic hormones, or drugs that block hormones, to change how an organism grows or functions.
A synthetic derivative of testosterone that increases muscle mass and strength.
A hormone made by the kidneys that stimulates red blood cell production.
The World Anti-Doping Agency, which bans performance-enhancing hormones in competitive sport.
A pill containing synthetic oestrogen and progesterone that prevents ovulation by inhibiting the release of FSH and LH.
Treatment that supplies oestrogen, often with progesterone, after the menopause.
A hormone that increases milk yield in cattle.
A plant hormone; synthetic auxins such as 2,4-D are used as selective weedkillers.
A plant hormone gas used to ripen fruit in storage.

questions.prompt: Give one example of the use of hormones in each of sport, health and agriculture, and explain the purpose of each.
questions.model: Sport: anabolic steroids, which are synthetic testosterone, increase muscle mass and strength and speed up recovery from training. Or EPO, which is made by the kidneys and stimulates red blood cell production, is used to increase the oxygen-carrying capacity of the blood and so endurance. Health: insulin injections treat type 1 diabetes, where the pancreas makes little or no insulin, so blood glucose is controlled. Or the contraceptive pill, containing synthetic oestrogen and progesterone, inhibits the release of FSH and LH so that ovulation is prevented. Agriculture: progesterone is used to synchronise the breeding cycles of cattle and sheep so that a herd gives birth at the same time. Or synthetic auxin 2,4-D is used as a selective weedkiller to kill broad-leaved weeds in cereal crops. Or ethene gas is used to ripen fruit such as bananas in storage.

questions.prompt: Evaluate the use of hormones in sport.
questions.model: Benefits: anabolic steroids increase muscle mass and strength and speed up recovery from training, and EPO increases the oxygen-carrying capacity of the blood, improving endurance. Costs: anabolic steroids cause liver damage, increase the risk of heart disease, reduce sperm production and infertility in males, cause male characteristics in females, acne and mood changes including aggression. EPO thickens the blood, increasing the risk of clots, heart attack and stroke. Their use is unfair to other competitors, so the World Anti-Doping Agency bans them in competitive sport and tests athletes through urine and blood samples. On balance, the health risks and the unfair advantage outweigh the benefits, which is why these hormones are banned.
